question.text: Chapter 6 emphasises that investors should closely monitor the QUANTUM OF INCENTIVE FEE because:

answer.text: A high incentive fee substantially reduces the NET return earned by investors
Higher incentive fees trigger lower GST automatically
Incentive fees above 25% are illegal under SEBI rules
High incentive fees guarantee higher GROSS returns

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6.3.3: 'A high pay-out of the Incentive Fees can substantially impact the Net Return earned by the investors. An AIF, making a high pay-out of Incentive Fees, will deliver decreasing Net Return on Investment, to the investors.' Gross return - fees = net return. The Trap: B is false (GST is flat 18%); C is false (no SEBI cap); D reverses cause and effect. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XIX-C test same. Gross vs net is the #1 LP metric to understand. Manager's Pro-Tip: In every LP report, quote NET IRR and NET MOIC alongside gross. A GP that hides net figures by quoting only gross is a transparency red flag — and sophisticated LPs catch this within one quarter of investor reporting.
